title: Photos & Frames
summary: My photography portfolio, where every image is monochrome until you show intent.
tagline: A home for my photography that feels like an exhibition rather than a feed: every photo appears in black and white and reveals its color on hover, focus, or touch.
role: Took the photographs and designed and built the site.
problem: Photographic work needs a focused, responsive presentation that lets the images carry the experience. A social feed crops, compresses, and surrounds them with noise.
contribution: I took the photographs and designed and built the site, including the workflow that prepares every original photo for the web.
solution: The site follows one visual rule: monochrome first, color on intent. The gallery is split into portraits, nature, and couples, each with a frame count and a full-screen lightbox with keyboard navigation. A services page covers photo editing, portfolio websites, custom galleries, and visual curation.
solutionPoints: A black-and-white-to-color reveal that works with a mouse, the keyboard, and touch.
An animated homepage composition, smooth scrolling, and page motion.
Lazy-loaded, web-ready images so an image-heavy page stays responsive.

architecture.summary: Original photos are prepared once, then reused across collections without duplication.
flow: Gallery: one collection at a time
Monochrome card → color on hover, focus, or touch

decisions.title: Make the reveal work for everyone.
decisions.text: Color responds to keyboard focus and taps as well as a mouse, so the core interaction works on every device.

decisions.title: Stay fast on a phone.
decisions.text: Images load as they are needed.

decisions.title: One photo, many collections.
decisions.text: A photograph can belong to more than one collection without being stored twice.

outcomes: Photos & Frames is live at photos.davishiggins.com as a purpose-built gallery for my photography.
limits: This is a separate project from wy_not_pics, which presents another photographer's work.
lessons: Gallery interactions should support attention to the images without making the photographs harder to reach.
